title: Salary Quartile Buckets Using NTILE
description:
Divide all employees into 4 equal salary quartile groups (1=lowest, 4=highest) using NTILE.

**Table: employees** — `id`, `name`, `salary`

Output columns: `name`, `salary`, `quartile`. Order by `salary`.
schema_sql: CREATE TABLE employees (id INT, name VARCHAR, salary INT); INSERT INTO employees VALUES (1,'Alice',45000),(2,'Bob',52000),(3,'Carol',61000),(4,'Dave',68000),(5,'Eve',75000),(6,'Frank',83000),(7,'Grace',91000),(8,'Henry',102000),(9,'Iris',115000),(10,'Jake',130000),(11,'Kim',145000),(12,'Leo',160000);
solution_sql: SELECT name, salary, NTILE(4) OVER (ORDER BY salary) AS quartile FROM employees ORDER BY salary

test_cases.description: 12 employees divided evenly into 4 quartiles of 3 employees each

hints: NTILE(4) divides the ordered rows into 4 buckets as evenly as possible, assigning bucket numbers 1 through 4.
With 12 rows and NTILE(4), each bucket gets exactly 3 rows; if rows don't divide evenly, earlier buckets get the extra row.
explanation: NTILE(n) divides the result set into n buckets. With 12 employees ordered by salary, NTILE(4) assigns quartile 1 to the 3 lowest earners (Alice 45k, Bob 52k, Carol 61k), quartile 2 to the next 3, and so on up to quartile 4 for the 3 highest earners. Useful for percentile-based segmentation.
